changes.reason: Evals and benchmarks need the exact messages the app sends; this renders them from app/main.py::chat without starting the server or calling the model.
changes.target: eval harness (all evals, prefix test, perf gate)
changes.risk: None at runtime: imported only by tests, evals and benchmarks.

changes.reason: Every request starts with the same ~982-token system prompt (estimated at 4 chars/token; built in `build_messages`, app/prompts.py:60), which the serving engine can serve from its prefix cache instead of recomputing. The vllm service `llm` has prefix caching enabled. A one-line change that puts a timestamp or request id at the top of this prompt would silently throw that away.

`create_ticket` (app/tickets.py:10) is guarded by `if not approved` on line 12, but nothing fails if a refactor removes it. This is the only thing standing between a model answer and an external side effect.
changes.risk: Test-only; outbound calls are patched to fail.

changes.reason: `openai.chat.completions.create` at app/llm.py:19 sets no timeout on the call or its client, so the openai SDK default (10 minutes) applies. A stalled stream holds the HTTP response open for the user for that whole time.
changes.risk: Requests slower than 60 s now fail instead of hanging; raise the value if your longest legitimate generation takes longer.

changes.reason: Keeps the timeout from being removed later.

`SYSTEM_PROMPT` is a 3,927-character string inlined in app/prompts.py:3. Edits to it are invisible in traces and eval results, so a quality change cannot be attributed to the prompt revision that caused it.
changes.risk: None: the loader returns the exact original text (verified byte-identical).

changes.reason: Load `SYSTEM_PROMPT` from prompts/system_prompt.md and expose `SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION` for traces and eval results.
changes.risk: Prompt text unchanged (verified byte-identical through the harness); the file must ship with the app.

changes.reason: `SYSTEM_PROMPT` (app/prompts.py:3) instructs the model to cite retrieved documents, but nothing checks that answers carry citations or that cited ids were actually retrieved.
changes.risk: Not run by plain pytest; Furnace Guard runs it against your endpoint.

changes.reason: Bootstrap dataset of real user questions for the citation and grounding evals.
Answers in this app are generated from retrieved documents (app/retriever.py:37). A citation can be present while the claim it supports is not in the cited text; only a semantic check catches that.
changes.risk: Advisory until calibrated against human labels.

changes.reason: The app is served by self-hosted vllm (--gpu-memory-utilization=0.70, --max-model-len=4096, --max-num-seqs=32, --enable-prefix-caching=True), but the repository has no load benchmark, so neither configuration changes nor code changes that alter prompt length can be compared against a known-good number.
Tells Furnace Guard which harness, evals, benchmarks and regression budget apply to this repository.
Runs the installed deterministic reliability tests on every pull request; no model or secrets required.
